chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥusayn al-ʿĀmirī, the client of Masʿūd ibn Mūsā, who said:

He narrated to me from one who asked him about a man who became in a state of janabah and could not obtain water, and the salat became due, so he performed tayammum with clean earth. Then he passed by water but did not perform ghusl, and waited for other water beyond that. Then the time of the later salat entered while he still had not reached the water, and he feared missing the salat. He said: “He performs tayammum and prays, for indeed his first tayammum was invalidated when he passed by the water and did not perform ghusl.”
As for the report narrated by Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who performed tayammum and prayed, then later obtained water, he said: “As for me, I would have done so; indeed I would perform wudu and repeat [the prayer].”

Its meaning is that if he had prayed at the beginning of the time, repetition is obligatory upon him. But if he had prayed at the end of the time, then there is no repetition of the salat upon him. That which indicates this is:
What the Shaykh—may Allah تعالى support him—reported to me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who performed tayammum and prayed, then after his prayer found water: should he perform wudu and repeat the salat, or is his salat valid? He said: “If he finds water before the time has passed, he performs wudu and repeats the salat; but if the time has passed, then there is no repetition upon him.”

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: clean earth or ground used for tayammum
key_terms.الْوَقْتُ: the appointed time of the salat
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum as a substitute purification

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water before the prayer time ends, must the salat be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings of tayammum for a person in janabah or without access to water, and when tayammum is invalidated by encountering water. It also addresses whether a prayer performed with tayammum must be repeated if water is later found, distinguishing between finding water before the prayer time ends and after it has passed. The passage is significant in fiqh for clarifying ritual purity and the validity or repetition of salat under changing circumstances.
